rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subdued the large, powerful sacrificial animals for human benefit, so people can lead, restrain, and slaughter them; without this subjection they would be no easier than wild beasts.
rows.anchor: فلا تستعصي عليكم حتى تأخذونها منقادة فتعقلونها وتحسبونها صافة قوائمها ثم تطعنون في لباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to give thanks calls people to thank God’s favor through drawing near to Him and acting sincerely.
rows.anchor: لتشكروا إنعامنا عليكم بالتقرب والإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the pagan custom of placing sacrificial blood around the Kaaba, the verse teaches that neither meat nor blood secures acceptance; what reaches God is the offerer’s God-conscious obedience and avoidance of unlawful or doubtful things.
rows.anchor: وهو قصد الائتمار وطلب الرضى والاحتراز عن الحرام والشبهة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that an act does not benefit without intention and sincerity.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه لا يفيد العمل بلا نية وإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s Coptic notables are singled out because the Israelites’ release depended on their opinions, not those of their descendants.
rows.anchor: أشراف قومه من القبط خصوا بالذكر لأن إرسال بني إسرائيل منوط بآرائهم لا بآراء أعقابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance meant refusing faith and obedience, treating God’s signs and messages lightly after their truth was clear, and considering themselves above accepting them.
rows.anchor: عن الإيمان والمتابعة وعظم الكبر أن يتهاون العبيد بآيات ربهم وبرسالاته بعد وضوحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were people whose habitual arrogance and rebellion exceeded all bounds.
rows.anchor: أي كانوا قوما عادتهم الاستكبار والتمرد {فقالوا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their response is grammatically joined to their arrogance, with the intervening phrase serving as a parenthetical confirmation; they spoke among themselves as if advising one another.
rows.anchor: عطف على استكبروا وما بينهما اعتراض مقرر للاستكبار أي قالوا فيما بينهم بطريق المناصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative in “shall we believe?” is a denial: they mean that they will not believe and that belief should not issue from them.
rows.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار بمعنى لا نؤمن وما ينبغي أن يصدر منا الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual description “like us” uses a form treated as a general verbal noun that applies to singular, dual, and plural, masculine and feminine.
rows.anchor: وصف بالمثل الاثنان لأنه في حكم المصدر العام للإفراد والتثنية والجمع المذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their people” means the Children of Israel; they are described as Pharaoh’s servants and dependents, as though enslaved, which the speakers use to lower Moses’ and Aaron’s standing below prophethood.
rows.anchor: يعنون بني إسرائيل {لنا} متعلقة بقوله : {عابدون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers meant to diminish the two messengers’ high rank by pointing to their people’s subordination to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: قصدوا بذلك التعرض لشأنهما وحط رتبتهما العلية عن منصب الرسالة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi relays a report found in some commentaries that the Children of Israel worshipped Pharaoh; the gloss says that such obedience would count as worship in reality.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در بعضى تفاسير آورده انده كه بني إسرائيل فرعون رامي رستيدند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron’s opponents persisted in denial until the two messengers despaired of their believing, and the people were drowned in the Sea of Qulzum.
rows.anchor: حتى يئسا من تصديقهم {فكانوا} فصاروا {من المهلكين} بالغرق في بحر القلزم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their destruction and Israel’s rescue, God gave Moses the Torah so the Children of Israel could find guidance by following its laws.
rows.anchor: {الكتاب} التوراة {لعلهم} لعل بني إسرائيل {يهتدون} إلى طريق الحق بالعمل بما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronting of “against them” before the subject hastens to show that the testimony harms them.
rows.anchor: تقديمه على الفاعل للمسارعة إلى بيان كون الشهادة ضارة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their tongues testify involuntarily before their mouths are sealed, so this does not conflict with the later statement that God seals mouths.
rows.anchor: وهذا قبل أن يختم على أفواههم فلا تعارض بينه وبين قوله تعالى : {اليوم نختم على أفواههم} (يس : 65)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every limb reports all the deeds its owner committed, not only the offense conventionally associated with that limb; the phrase refers to all their evil acts.
rows.anchor: فتخبر كل جارحة بما صدر من أفاعيل صاحبها لا أن كلا منها تخبر بجنايتها المعهودة فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Recompense” means repayment, “full” means complete, and “true” qualifies the recompense: God gives them the complete, established punishment they deserve when their limbs testify.
rows.anchor: التوفية بذل الشيء وافيا والوافي الذي بلغ التمام والدين الجزاء والحق منصوب على أن يكون صفة للدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they see the terrors, they will know God is manifestly true because He has made plain the truth of the recompense He promised in worldly life.
rows.anchor: عند معاينتهم الأهوال والخطوب {أن الله هو الحق المبين} أي الظاهر حقيته لما أنه أبان لهم حقية ما كان يعدهم به في الدنيا من الجزاء.

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali identifies disbelief, religious innovation, and sinfulness as the three qualities that warrant cursing, and divides each into three levels.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي رحمه الله الصفات المقتضية للعن ثلاث الكفر والبدعة والفسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cursing broad classes or more specific groups is permitted, but cursing ambiguous innovator categories is risky; absent a transmitted wording, common people should avoid it to prevent reciprocal cursing and conflict.
rows.anchor: ولكن في لعن بعض أصناف المبتدعة خطر لأن معرفة البدعة غامضة فما لم يرد فيه لفظ مأثور ينبغي أن يمنع منه العوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A named person may be cursed if religious law establishes that he died in disbelief and doing so harms no Muslim; Pharaoh, Nimrod, and Abu Jahl are examples.
rows.anchor: إن كان ممن ثبت كفره شرعا فيجوز لعنه إن لم يكن فيه أذى على مسلم كقولك لعنة الله على النمرود وفرعون وأبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cursing an individual whose final state is unknown is dangerous, since a Jew or sinner may convert or repent and die near to God.
rows.anchor: فهذا فيه خطر لأنه ربما يسلم أو يتوب فيموت مقربا عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day is hard and full of terrors for disbelievers, while God’s grace makes it easy for believers; a hadith says it will feel lighter to a believer than a prescribed prayer performed in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في الحديث : "إنه يهون يوم القيامة على المؤمن حتى يكون أخف عليه من صلاة مكتوبة صلاها في الدنيا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers experience the Day as severe because of Hell and regret for lost gardens after worldly ease; believers who seek and strive meet the gardens and the Merciful after accepting hardship and trusting that ease follows hardship.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن الكافرين يرون ذلك اليوم عسيرا عظيما من دخول النار وحسرة فوات الجنان

rows.speaker: سهل الصعلوكي
rows.claim: When a Jew asked whether worldly life is the believer’s prison and the disbeliever’s paradise, Sahl replied that it is paradise for one sent to God’s punishment and prison for one sent to God’s bliss.
rows.anchor: فقال سهل على البداهة : إذا صرت إلى عذاب الله كانت هذه جنتك وإذا صرت إلى نعيم الله كانت هذه سجني

rows.speaker: الشبلي
rows.claim: Asked when salvation is possible amid worldly occupations and afterlife terrors, al-Shibli answered: leave worldly occupations and you will be safe from afterlife terrors.
rows.anchor: وقيل للشبلي رحمه الله : في الدنيا أشغال وفي الآخرة أهوال فمتى النجاة؟ قال : دع أشغالها تأمن من أهوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persian verse likens the world to cheap carrion and asks why one should be greedy for such refuse; the lesson is to abandon attachment to it.
rows.anchor: اين جهان جيفه است ومردار ورخيص برنين مردار وان باشم حريص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual seekers uproot love of everything besides God and endure the rigors of striving until they reach the ease they seek.
rows.anchor: وقلعوا من قلوبهم أصل حب ما سوى الله تعالى ونصبوا نفوسهم لمقاساة شدائد الجهاد إلى أن يصلوا إلى اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also signals that deniers who slandered God’s saints to drive people away from them for worldly gain will be helpless on that Day, forced to confess and renew faith by saying there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: أهل الإنكار يلقون يوم القيامة عسرا لأنهم وقعوا في أعراض الأولياء في الدنيا تنفيرا للناس عنهم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators hold that this verse was abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : هذه منسوخة بآية السيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do you suppose” means “rather, do you think”; true hearing is hearing the recited signs, while understanding means grasping their admonitions and calls to virtue.
rows.anchor: من المواعظ الزاجرة عن القبائح الداعية إلى المحاسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Most” is specified because some did believe or recognize the truth but resisted it to protect their leadership.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الأكثر لأنه كان منهم من آمن ومنهم من عقل الحق وكابر استدبارا وخوفا على الرياسة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says a caller’s words reach people only if they heard the primordial call; their response to the prophet is a blessing of that pre-eternal response, while heedlessness reflects their distance from its source.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : لا تظن أنك تسمع نداءك إنما تسمعهم إن سمعوا نداء الأزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble livestock because they gain no benefit from revealed warnings or observed proofs, remaining heedless and misguided.
rows.anchor: ما يقرع آذانهم من قوارع الآيات وانتفاء التدبر فيما يشاهدونه من الدلائل والمعجزات {إلا كالانعام}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmī Interpretations says their only appetite is food, drink, and satisfying the ego’s desires, like livestock.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : ليس لهم نهمة إلا في الأكل والشرب واستجلاب حظوظ النفس كالبهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock follow whoever guides them, recognize benefactors, seek what helps, and avoid what harms; these people neither submit to their Lord nor distinguish His beneficence from Satan’s harm, seek reward, or avoid punishment.
rows.anchor: لأنها تنقاد لمن يقودها وتميز من يحسن إليها وتطلب ما ينفعها وتجتنب ما يضرها وهؤلاء لا ينقادون لربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals hold no beliefs and acquire no good or evil, whereas these people do; human ignorance also provokes strife and turns others from the truth.
rows.anchor: ولأنها لم تعتقد حقا ولم تكتسب خيرا ولا شرا بخلاف هؤلاء ولأن جهالتها لا تضر بأحد وجهالة هؤلاء تؤدي إلى هيج الفتن وصد الناس عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals cannot seek perfection and so are not negligent or blameworthy, whereas people can and are culpable for neglect deserving severe punishment.
rows.anchor: ولأنها غير متمكنة من طلب الكمال فلا تقصير منها ولاذم وهؤلاء مقصرون مستحقون أعظم العقاب على تقصيرهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created angels with reason, beasts with appetite, and humans with both; when appetite overcomes reason a person is worse than beasts, while reason overcoming appetite makes a person like the angels.
rows.anchor: خلق الملائكة وعلى العقل جبلهم وخلق البهائم وركب فيها الشهوة وخلق الإنسان وركب فيه الأمرين أي العقل والشهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who masters his own desires is better than the angels, as the verse about the best of creation states.
rows.anchor: ومن كان غالبا على أمره فهو خير من الملائكة كما قال تعالى : {أولئك هم خير البرية} (البين : 7)

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawi depicts angels as reason and worship without appetite, beasts as appetite without knowledge, and humans as divided between an upward and downward pull.
rows.anchor: خير البرية} (البين : 7) كما قال في "المثنوي".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Merciful” is the predicate of an omitted subject, identifying the Creator of the heavens, earth, and what lies between them; this prepares for the command to prostrate in 25:60 and interprets the mentioned establishment as a rank of mercy.
rows.anchor: وبيان أن المراد من الاستواء المذكور في الحقيقة تعيين مرتبة الرحمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “who created” attaches to “expert”: ask an expert about creation and establishment, meaning the Creator Himself knows His acts and attributes; the author cites 9:117 and 35:14 and discusses the reading of 3:7 that includes those firmly grounded in knowledge.
rows.anchor: متعلق بما بعده وهو {خبيرا} كما في قوله : {إنه بهم رءوف رحيم} (التوبة : 117)

rows.speaker: الفتوحات المكية
rows.claim: The Meccan Revelations explains that God, though beyond place, created the Throne and described Himself as established upon it as a merciful direction for supplication, since embodied hearts need a direction; all things serve spiritual ranks rather than themselves.
rows.anchor: وفي "الفتوحات المكية" : لما كان الحق تعالى هو السلطان الأعظم ولا بد للسلطان من مكان يكون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate is addressed to the polytheists; prostration here means prayer, named for its greatest pillar, and the Merciful is the One whose mercy brought all beings into existence.
rows.anchor: {وإذا قيل لهم} أي لهؤلاء المشركين {اسجدوا} صلوا وعبر عن الصلاة بالسجدة لأنها من أعظم أركانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question “what is the Merciful?” asks about the bearer of the name: they either did not know it was a name of God, or knew that but suspected it could refer to another person.
rows.anchor: لأن وضع ما أعم وهو سؤال عن المسمى بهذا الاسم لأنهم ما كانوا يطلقونه على الله ولا يعرفون كونه تعالى مسمى بهذا الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says they exploited the name’s association with Musaylima, known as the Merciful of Yamama, to insinuate that Muhammad ordered worship of him; he compares this equivocation to hypocrites claiming they had only been joking about the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : إن محمدا يأمرنا بعبادة رحمن اليمامة ونظيره أن المنافقين صدرت منهم كلمات وحركات

rows.speaker: ابن طلحة
rows.claim: Ibn Ṭalḥa defines equivocation as using a word with a similar or opposite meaning that better serves the speaker’s intent to obscure what is meant.
rows.anchor: أحسن موقعا لإرادته الإبهام به كذا في "العقد الفريد" للعلامة ابن طلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Shall we prostrate to what you command?” means they refuse to bow to the Merciful without knowing who He is.
rows.anchor: بسجوده من غير أن نعرف أن المسجود له ماذا وهو استفهام إنكار أي لا نسجد للرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses the thing that increased them as the command to prostrate to the Merciful.
rows.anchor: {وزادهم} أي الأمر بالسجود للرحمن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their recoil is a retreat and distancing from faith, as in the parallel statement in Noah 71:6.
rows.anchor: والنفور الانزعاج عن الشيء والتباعد وهو نظير قوله : {فلم يزدهم دعآءى إلا فرارا} (نوح : 6)

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fath al-Raḥmān says that denying the Merciful’s existence, or knowingly doing or saying something that only an unbeliever would do or say, constitutes unbelief by consensus; such acts mark denial.
rows.anchor: فمن جهل وجود الرحمن أو علم وجوده وفعل فعلا أو قال قولا لا يصدر إلا من كافر فكافر بالاتفاق كما في "فتح الرحمن"

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: When reciting the verse, Sufyan al-Thawri raised his head to heaven and said that the enemies’ increased aversion made him more humble before God.
rows.anchor: وكان سفيان الثوري رحمه الله إذا قرأ هذه الآية رفع رأسه إلى السماء وقال : إلهي زادني خضوعا ما زاد أعداءك نفورا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A man asked the Prophet to pray that he might accompany him in Paradise; the Prophet told him to help him by prostrating often.
rows.anchor: صلى الله عليه وسلم ادع الله أن يرزقني مرافقتك في الجنة قال : "أعني بكثرة السجود".

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fath al-Raḥmān says this verse is unanimously a place for prostration of recitation.
rows.anchor: قال في "فتح الرحمن" : وهذا محل سجود بالاتفاق.

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says this is the seventh recitation prostration according to Abu Hanifa and the eighth according to al-Shafiʿi; he notes its name as the prostration of recoil and denial, and connects the believer’s prostration with distinction from deniers.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (اين سجدة هفتم است بقول إمام اعظم وبقول إمام شافعي سجدة هشتم واين را در فتوحات سجدة نفور وانكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authorities differ over whether the takbir for recitation prostration is sunnah, recommended, or whether the second takbir is a pillar; the source says both takbirs are not pillars.
rows.anchor: وتكبير سجود تلاوة سنة كما في "النهاية" أو ندب كما في "الكافي" أو الثاني ركن كما في "الزاهدي" ولم يوجد أن كليهما ركن

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf treats a delayed recitation prostration as make-up and requires it immediately; the author says it is not immediate in their school and may be performed throughout life except at disliked times.
rows.anchor: كما قال أبو يوسف فهو على الفور عنده لكنه ليس على الفور عندنا فجميع العمر وقته سوى المكروه

rows.speaker: الطحاوي
rows.claim: Al-Tahawi says delaying the prostration is disliked; al-Tajnis calls this the sounder view, as cited by al-Qahistani.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطحاوي أنه مكروه وهو الأصح كما في "التجنيس" ذكره القهستاني في "شرحه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate to the Merciful means there is no prostration to anyone else; otherwise a wife would have been commanded to prostrate to her husband.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن لا سجدة لغير الرحمن ولو كانت لأمرت المرأة بسجدة زوجها

rows.speaker: شمس الأئمة السرخسي
rows.claim: Al-Sarakhsī says prostrating to anyone other than God as an act of reverence is unbelief, and kissing the ground before scholars is forbidden.
rows.anchor: قال شمس الأئمة السرخسي : السجود لغير الله تعالى على وجه التعظيم كفر وما يفعلونه من تقبيل الأرض بين يدي العلماء فحرام.

rows.speaker: الصدر الشهيد
rows.claim: Al-Ṣadr al-Shahīd says such prostration is not unbelief if intended as greeting, but it still should not be done because that is an abrogated practice from Jacob’s time, when prostration served as greeting, as in Joseph 12:100.
rows.anchor: وذكر الصدر الشهيد : لا يكفر بهذا السجود لأنه يريد به التحية انتهى لكنه يلزم عليه أن لا يفعل لأنه شريعة منسوخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses encourage the suffering to remain patient and not despair, since hardship’s dark night will give way to the day of fortune; the author prays for wakefulness, witnessing, and release from existential darkness and deprivation.
rows.anchor: آرام داريد ايمن مباشيد كه شب محنت بر اثرست واى كساني كه اندر تاريكي شب محنت بي آرام بوده آيد نوميد مباشيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Merciful’s servants are unlike servants of worldly life, Satan, the ego, or desire: though all creatures are servants by creation, only those with the following qualities merit this honorific title as recipients of special mercy.
rows.anchor: دون عباد الدنيا والشيطان والنفس والهوى فإنهم وإن كانوا عبادا بالإيجاد لكنهم ليسوا بأهل لإضافة التشريف والتفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are God’s accepted servants; “walking” is intentional movement between places, while “hawn” means calm dignity, humility without disgrace, and gentle softness.
rows.anchor: والمعنى عباده المقبولون وهو مبتدأ خبره قوله : {الذين يمشون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They walk calmly and humbly, without pride, show, or tyranny, because contemplating God’s greatness and majesty humbles their spirits, selves, and bodies.
rows.anchor: يمشون بسكينة وتواضع لا بفخر وفرح ورياء وتجبر وذلك لما طالعوا من عظمة الحق وهيبته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith likens believers’ gentle obedience to a nose-pierced camel that follows when led and kneels when made to kneel; the text explains the animal’s docility through pain from its nose ring.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "المؤمنون هينون لينون كالجمل الأنف إن قيد انقاد وإن أنيخ على صخرة استناخ"

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A second wording compares the believer to a camel that follows when led and kneels when made to kneel; the commentary explains the grammar of “led” and “made to kneel.”
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "المؤمن كالجمل إن قيد انقاد وإن استنيخ على صخرة استناخ"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sahih lexicon explains that the camel described as anaf has a painful nose from its nose ring; the commentary uses this pain to explain its docility.
rows.anchor: وفي "الصحاح" أنف البعير اشتكى أنفه من البرة فهو أنف ككتف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignorance includes lacking knowledge, believing contrary to reality, or acting contrary to what one ought to do, even with a correct belief; deliberately abandoning prayer is an example, and 2:67 calls mockery ignorance.
rows.anchor: الجهل خلو النفس من العلم واعتقاد الشيء بخلاف ما هو عليه وفعل الشيء بخلاف ما حقه أن يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the ignorant are fools who address the servants of the Merciful face-to-face with vile speech.
rows.anchor: والمعنى وإذا كلمهم السفهاء مواجهة بالكلام القبيح

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: One interpretation reads “peace” as asking for safety, with an omitted verb governing the accusative expression.
rows.anchor: أي نطلب منكم السلامة فيكون منصوبا باضمار فعل كما في "المفردات"

rows.speaker: إحياء العلوم
rows.claim: Another interpretation means: we are safe from your sin, and you are safe from our harm.
rows.anchor: أو إنا سلمنا من إثمكم وأنتم سلمتم من شرنا كما في "إحياء العلوم"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take “peace” as a verbal noun standing for “we take leave from you,” meaning they do not answer foolishness in kind.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : سلاما مصدر فعل محذوف أقيم مقام التسلم أي قالوا : نتسلم منكم تسلما أي لا نجاهلكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They avoid foolish dealings and keep neither friendship nor hostility with such people; most commentators say “peace” describes an omitted statement rather than their literal wording, meaning they avoid harm, sin, argument, and debate.
rows.anchor: والمعنى قالوا قولا سلاما أي سدادا يسلمون فيه من الأذى والإثم (مراد ترك تعرض سفهاست

rows.speaker: المحقق الرومي
rows.claim: The Rumi couplet advises leaving when called ostentatious or hypocritical and responding to angry insults with prayer, good cheer, and departure.
rows.anchor: كما قال المحقق الرومي : اكر كويند زراقى وسالوس بكوهستم دوصد ندان وميرو

rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdi’s story tells of a drunk who broke a patient man’s head with a lute at night; the next day the injured man gives him money and excuses his drunkenness, saying his own wound healed but the drunk’s will heal only with money.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره : يكى بربطى دربغل داشت مست بشب درسر ارسايى شكست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line about God’s friends says they endure abundant wrong from people; the verse’s “when” clause then describes their conduct with others after their inner qualities have been described.
rows.anchor: اذان دوستان خدا بر سرند كه از خلق بسيار بر خرخورند ثم إن قوله : (وإذا) بيان لحالهم في المعاملة مع غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies Pharaoh as al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab, kunya Abu al-ʿAbbās; another report gives his name as Mughib and kunya Abu Murra, and says he lived 460 years.
rows.anchor: وهو الوليد بن مصعب وكنيته أبو العباس وقيل : اسمه مغيب وكنيته أبو مرة وعاش أربعمائة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each of the two messengers says, “We are the messenger of the Lord of the worlds”; another view explains the singular “messenger” because Moses alone was independently a messenger and Aaron supported and followed him.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لم يقل رسولا لأن موسى كان الرسول المستقل بنفسه وهارون كان ردأ يصدقه تبعا له في الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Release the Children of Israel with us” explains the message’s command: let them go free to Syria, the land where their ancestors had lived.
rows.anchor: والإرسال ههنا التخلية والإطلاق كما تقول : أرسلت الكلب إلى الصيد أي خلهم وشأنهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Pharaoh had enslaved the Israelites for 400 years; they then numbered 630,000. Moses returned to Egypt, where Aaron was, and together they went to Pharaoh’s gate at night; one report says Pharaoh admitted them immediately, while another says he waited until morning.
rows.anchor: وكان فرعون استعبدهم أربعمائة سنة وكانوا في ذلك الوقت ستمائة ألف وثلاثين ألفا فانطلق موسى إلى مصر وهارون كان بها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: At the gate Moses announced he was the Lord of the worlds’ messenger; the porter called him mad, and al-Suddī says Pharaoh admitted them at once, while another account has Pharaoh summon them in the morning; they delivered God’s message and Pharaoh recognized and insulted Moses, whom he had raised.
rows.anchor: كما قاله السدي أو ترك حتى أصبح ثم دعاهما فدخلا عليه وأديا رسالة الله فعرف فرعون موسى لأنه نشأ في بيته فشتمه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Moses and Aaron waited a year at Pharaoh’s gate; Pharaoh finally admitted them to laugh at them, then recognized Moses after hearing the message and asked whether he had not raised him as a child.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : إنهما انطلقا إلى باب فرعون فلم يؤذن لهما سنة حتى قال البواب : ههنا إنسان

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses the question as “Did we not raise you among us when you were a child?” and describes him as close to newborn age.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (نه ترا رورديم درميان خويش {وليدا} در حالتي كه طفل بودي نزديك بولادت)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Child” describes him because he was near the time of birth; “of your lifetime” is a circumstantial phrase modifying “years.”
rows.anchor: عبر عن الطفل بذلك لقرب عهده من الولادة.

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines a lifespan as the period, short or long, during which the body is inhabited by life.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : العمر اسم لمدة عمارة البدن بالحياة قليلة أو كثيرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One chronology says Moses lived 30 years among Pharaoh’s people, spent 10 years in Midian, returned to call them to God for 30 years, and lived 50 years after the drowning, totaling 120 years.
rows.anchor: قيل : لبث فيهم ثلاثين سنة ثم خرج إلى مدين وأقام بها عشر سنين ثم عاد إليهم يدعوهم إلى الله تعالى ثلاثين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s “deed” refers to Moses killing Pharaoh’s baker, named Fatun; after recalling Moses’ upbringing, Pharaoh invokes and magnifies the killing.
rows.anchor: الفعلة بالفتح المرة الواحدة يعني قتل القبطي الذي كان خباز فرعون واسمه فاتون

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says the deed’s magnification is conveyed by not naming it directly, since making something indefinite or obscure can serve to magnify it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : تعظيم تلك الفعلة يستفاد من عدم التصريح باسمها الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “you are among the ungrateful” is circumstantial and means Moses denied Pharaoh’s favor and the right due to his upbringing.
rows.anchor: حال من إحدى التاءين أي من المنكرين لنعمتي والجاحدين لحق تربيتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he did the deed at the time he killed the man; “then” functions only as a response particle because a causal reading is remote.
rows.anchor: {إذا} أي حين فعلت أي قتلت النفس وهو حرف جواب فقط لأن ملاحظة المجازاة ههنا بعيدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among the astray” means Moses missed the right course unintentionally, like aiming at a bird but striking a person; he intended to discipline the man, not kill him.
rows.anchor: ضللت طريق الصواب وأخطأته من غير تعمد كمن رمى سهما إلى طائر وأصاب آدميا وذلك لأن مراد موسى كان تأديبه لا قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fled to Midian fearing for his life and fearing they would harm him and punish him beyond what his offense deserved.
rows.anchor: {لما خفتكم} أن تصيبوني بمضرة وتؤاخذوني بما لا أستحقه بجنايتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted Moses knowledge and wisdom when he returned from Midian and made him a messenger to Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: حين رجعت من مدين. {حكما} أي علما وحكمة {وجعلنى من المرسلين} إليكم.

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fath al-Raḥmān interprets “judgment” as prophethood and being made a messenger as a further rank, since some prophets are not messengers.
rows.anchor: وفي "فتح الرحمن" : حكما أي نبوة وجعلني من المرسلين درجة ثانية للنبوة فرب نبي ليس برسول.

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some Sufi masters say that when God intends to raise someone to a high station, He casts fear on him so he flees from people and God unveils the secrets special to him.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : إن الله تعالى إذا أراد أن يبلغ أحدا من خلقه إلى مقام من المقامات العالية يلقي عليه رعبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elect’s errors are unlike ordinary people’s sins: they arise from mistake rather than natural desire, and such error is forgiven.
rows.anchor: ومعاصي الخواص ليست كمعاصي غيرهم فإنهم لا يقعون فيها بحكم الشهوة الطبيعية بل بحسب الخطا وذلك مرفوع
